title: Pb(II) Removal From Aqueous Solutions Using Differently Sourced and Processed Lythrum salicaria Biomass: Adsorption Kinetics, Isotherm Models, and Thermodynamics
content:
This study offers original contributions by comparing differently sourced and processed biomass forms of L. salicaria and systematically analyzing their adsorption efficiencies using established kinetic and isotherm models. The results demonstrate that L. salicaria-originated biomasses have strong potential as an alternative biosorbent for heavy metal remediation.


ABSTRACT

In this study, the Pb(II) removal potential of Lythrum salicaria L. in its differently sourced and processed forms was investigated in a batch system. The characterization of biosorbents was performed by zeta potential measurements, BET analysis, FT-IR spectroscopy, and SEM–EDX analyses. pH, biosorbent dosage, contact time, temperature, and initial metal concentration were the parameters studied to optimize the biosorption process. Isotherm and kinetic models were used to elucidate the mechanism of lead biosorption onto plant-based adsorbents. It was determined that the experimental data obtained with each biosorbent best fit the Langmuir isotherm model. The maximum monolayer biosorption capacity for HCB, DRB, SAECB, SAB, and EB was found to be 100.82 (25°C), 139.96 (25°C), 226.70 (45°C), 120.19 (45°C), and 163.67 mg/g (45°C), respectively. The pseudo–second-order kinetic model was determined to be applicable for all processes, and the nature of the processes was defined to be spontaneous because Gibbs energy values are negative. Overall, L. salicaria grown at hydroponic culture and nature and its modified variants show significant potential as biosorbents in the treatment of Pb(II) contaminated aqueous systems.
